## f7660051ec70

**Classification: domain question / possible shortcut — active-frame seed
multiplicities never compose within one grid.**

Audited generator SHA-256:
`ebf6a3812da68f57f361fa3058c190d4da0828a28b429c6d578dbe1976a20b5a`;
declared rule hash `3efd212303b7`. The portable suite passed 53/53. The combined
audit command exited 1 only because its strict semantic stage requires a
separate declared-period receipt. The prescribed fixed-seed period census then
covered all 6 easy/medium/hard start-residue lessons and all 24 query rotations
with zero production or rotation ambiguities, no hook warnings, and no scoring
errors:
`checks/audit/f7660051ec70-schedule-period.summary.json`.

A separate composition gap remains. All seeded frames in each generated grid
share the one global `seed_count`. Across 1,024 deterministic draws (`None`,
easy, medium, hard; indices 0–255; seed `200000 + index`), zero grids mixed a
one-seed and a two-seed active frame. A rival that fills only active frames whose
seed count matches the first active frame therefore matched the selected Python
rule on all 1,024 sampled inputs.

The retained 9x11 counterexample contains one one-seed active frame, one
two-seed active frame, and one empty decoy. It passes `self_check`, and
`observe_overrides` reports `seed_count="mixed"`. The canonical Racket rule
fills both active interiors; the rival fills only the first. Exact evidence:

- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70/finding.json`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70/input.json`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70/racket.json`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70/rival.json`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70/reproduce.py`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70-combined/result.json`
- `checks/audit/f7660051ec70-schedule-period.summary.json`

Replay from packet root:

```text
python3 review.py run python3 ../checks/audit/f7660051ec70/reproduce.py
```

The owner notes explicitly chose uniform per-grid counts to retain a simple
axis, so this is reported as a domain/curriculum question rather than a label
bug. If mixed active-frame counts are intended to be outside training scope,
the validator or an explicit training-domain contract should say so. The target
was not modified.
